If you were a fan of the original Blackguards, you'll find much to love in the new release. There are beloved  characters (Naurim, Zurbaran, et al.)  making their returns, and an all-new story of politics and revenge.
Some of the awkward aspects of the first release have been addressed.
Lasting wounds no longer require in-town healers to fix. In the previous game, this was a well-intentioned incentive to play well, but typically turned into a money/time sync. It's gone. Good riddance.
While the story still follows a relatively linear arc, the overworld map has many more nodes than before, representing land held by you and your opponent. If you and your armies can overtake these nodes, they unlock valuable bonuses and paths to new dungeons. Be warned, they can also be re-taken by your opponent, forcing you to re-take those nodes.
This allows a bit more variety than before. Instead of strictly puzzle-based handcrafted levels, you can now "grind" a little bit for XP and fun. This was sorely missed in the original game. It's not a complete solution, but alleviates a lot the pain.
The game has been simplified to make it more appealing to the less hardcore tabletop gamers. Skill trees are streamlined and some of the more cryptic stats have been brought in to the light.
You will also find levels that can be treated more as a tactical match instead of a puzzle whose trick needs to be figured out. In other words, the previous game had only one or two "correct" ways to finish a fight. This restriction has been loosened somewhat - although not to the degree that it should have.

I remember the time that me and my friend came across these two sick and dying patients in a doctor's house. The nurse there had a healing stone, but it had only enough charge to cure one of the patients.
The other would die.
We realised this was no light choice. We had these two people lives in our hands, and one of them was about to slip away.
We spent the next few minutes gathering information about both of these people. Anything that might help us decide.
The answer became clearer.
I figured we should save the man with a family, who is well loved and respected around the town. I was, in fact, surprised to learn that my friend felt differently. He though that we should save the young travelling merchant because he "liked the way he looked".
How arbitrary.
It seemed we weren't going to reach an agreement. It seems we would have to agree to disagree and then leave it up to the flip of a coin to see who to save.
But my friend wasn't content with that.
He drew his bow and walked right up to the older man's bed and threatened to shoot unless we did things his way.
I knew he wasn't bluffing.
Unwilling to compromise for the sake of a merchant without a family who risked his life every time he left the town gates, I knocked my friend to the ground, thereby eliminating the immediate threat he posed.
I had only a few moments to convince him to do this the fair way... But I failed.
We both knew I had superior equipment, and so I hoped that would deter my friend from attacking me. The problem was that he would do anything to get his way most times, and I knew this.
And so we fought.
"Don't make me do this!"
"I'm not."
"If you keep trying to kill that man, I'll have no choice!"
"Just let him die! He's useless!"
"Stop it! I don't want to have to waste another resurrection scroll on you, but if you die I'll be the only one to make the call!"
"You wouldn't do that!"
"And why not? Besides, your guy still has a chance to live! As big a chance as my guy!"
"Ok! Ok... You have a point. We'll do it the "fair" way."
Relief! I had convinced him. It was a lucky thing, too. He was on the ground, about to die.
We played a game of scissors paper rock. Honestly... I cheated. We were in the same room and I waited to hear the sound effect that indicated which option he chose. He didn't notice and I didn't tell him until the ordeal was over.
And so the well-known, loved and respected man was the one who was healed. I could tell my friend was annoyed but his clutching his hair and saying "No!"
And that was that.
Except it wasn't.
I couldn't believe what I was seeing... The man was just about to walk out of the house when my friend shot him! He didn't die immediately, but I knew I couldn't stop him this time. Even if I killed him, I'd just be wasting a resurrection scroll... My friend wouldn't stop until the other man was dead.
And so I said "Fine!"
I drew my dagger and went to the side of the other man's bed. I thrust the dagger down once, twice, and it was over. There was blood all over the floor, and all over the bed. We looked at each other. "You monster..." I said.
And then we burst out into laughter.

Arson & Plunder: Unleashed
Beat'em Up
Chainsaw Syndicate
Headup Games
is a 2D Beat'em Up developed by Chainsaw Syndicate and published by Headup Games.
During a war between elves and orcs, humans start deforesting their land. So, orcs and elves make a truce and send their two best warriors to save the forest. However, these warriors get stuck together in a way vary similar to Trine, and they are forced to cooperate to stop the humans from accomplishing their plans.
Okay, I'm gonna be honest with you: the story is very simple, but also quite funny. There is a lot of humor that has more hits than misses, and I had a good time watching the cutscenes and the beginning and end of each level.
The 2D artstyle is very colorful and detailed, as well as not being a confusing mess. However, the background tends to get repetitive in each level.
The game is a sidescrolling beat'em up that features normal and special attacks as well as switching your character on the fly: the elf is more suited to long-range combat, while the orc is better for melee fights. I am not a big fan of this genre, but I had quite a blast playing this game: thanks to the simple controls and the fluid combat, I have beaten the entire thing in one section with a friend beside me. And that's the best way to enjoy this: with a human friend next to you.
The game is, sadly, pretty easy: most of the times you'll be able to fend off enemies by spamming the attack button, and if the enemies get too close, one of the special attacks will defeat them quite easily.
I despise repetitive soundtracks, and they usually ruin a game for me. But here, I was pleasantly surprised: the rock music featured in the game enhances the frenetic action, making every situation better than I could've ever imagined when I first started the game. Props to the music composer.
Other than getting all the achievements, playing Endless mode and beating the game with a friend, there isn't that big a lasting appeal.
Overall, this is a damn good beat'em up with a kickass score, fun story and enjoyable gameplay that is only improved by the presence of cooperative gameplay. I recommend this to fans of the genre and newcomers alike.

Grim Dawn is the game that i wanted, but didn't get from Diablo 3.
If you are a fan of Action RPGs, this is probably for you. It's the best attempt I've played in about a decade - since what i would call the glory days of the genre, when Diablo 2 and Titan Quest were among my top played games. Which is just what this game reminds me of - everything great about the Diablo and Titan Quest franchises mushed up into one new product with a new world and some small quality of life enhancements. This game was clearly designed for fans of those games - you don't have to take my word for it, you can still go to the developers forums and look - they actively asked for input from backers, and listened! And boy did it work!
I'm not trying to say that Torchlight, Path of Exile, or Diablo 3 are bad. I'm just saying Grim Dawn personally tickles a particular itch that those games did not. If you are looking for that late 90s / early 2000's style point-and-click action RPG loot fest, this is it. Heck, If you've ever liked any action RPG, this is worth checking out.
Pros:
+Plenty of Diversity in Character Builds - 6 Skill trees to put experience points into while leveling, of which two can be unlocked by one character, plus a web of "devotion" unlocks for more passive buffs and extra abilities as rewards for exploration.
+Tons of loot. Game includes a filter to hide / show only certain grades or above of loot, for when your character is already well equipped and you dont want to pick up and lug junk back to sell off.
+All items are augmentable, and there are tons of Augment Components to slot into weapons and armor, again adding to diversity.
+Gorgeous hand-crafted world. The game engine might not be the best, but it renders the world gloriously.
+Satisfying Combat. Just smacking baddies with a sword has the right visuals and sounds to make it feel great - spells and abilities make it even better, just killing things for hours on end is fun and feels great.
+LAN mode. You never know when you might want to take a few friends and some laptops to the woods to play a game, no internet connection is required, you can host local lobbies without doing any work arounds or sneaky things, even with the steam version of the game.
+Controller Support. I mean, i think you are insane if you want to use a controller to play this game, but, it's there!
+Moddable. There are already several great mods out there, expanding gameplay options, adding new skill trees, items, and more. One mod adds a Necromancer class, for example. Another adds all the classes from Titan Quest.
+Ongoing development. While the game has made it to its final release, there are still hotfix patches coming out, and an expected expansion pack - this game should have legs, and support will likely be around for a while.
Cons:
- Hand-Crafted World. There is some randomization in where obstructions and secret areas appear, but as of now there is virtualy no randomly generated content. (Rumor is a patch, DLC, or Expansion may add this.) For some people this may limit gameplay, as exploration wont have the same appeal since most of the world is exactly the same.
- Visibility Issues - Most games of the ARPG variety use an isometric, fixed camera angle. Grim Dawn allows more freedom, and sometimes this means unusual angles and obstructions may cause enemies to be hard to see, or the rotation of the camera to throw off your environmental awareness.
- No Character Cosmetic Options Other Than Gear - When you make a character, you pick male or female. Thats it. No customization of the appearance at all. While some items exist to paint an illusion on top of an item to make it look different, the system seems limited - certainly nowhere near as robust as Diablo 3's Transmogrify system.

Never before have I played a game where I can actually shoot my music.  But seriously, this game is awesome! If only they made this portable so we could blast the heck our music on our iOS devices anywhere we go...OH, WAIT.  There is!  There's also an iOS version of this game that you can take anywhere and play the tracks on your iPod Touch or similar iOS device.  Granted, that version is a BIT scaled down, but it retains the fun and replayabilty of the PC/Mac version, more or less.  But the compatability is not even the best part...

So you SHOULD play it with a gamepad. x3  And the graphics, while a bit limited in terms of 2D sprites, are very vibrant and colorful thanks to all the pryotechnics and lights that actually sync up to your music!  Is it too bright?  Turn the intensity down!  Do you want more color and lights?  Then, turn the intensity up more!
And not only do you get vivid graphics, great controls, and limitless replayabilty, but you also get a good handful of ships to unlock and play as.  And all of them play differently, each with their own varying styles of play.  In addition to the already substansial selection of playiable ships in the vanilla version, you can upgrade to the Ultra version and get more ships, more gameplay variety, more everything!  Not to mention that there is also the Shadow Ops DLC which adds even MORE ships and a new layer of gameplay!  But wait...did I mention this game has full Steam Workshop support as well?  Soooo...you get even MOOOORE ships to play as in addition to what the base game and DLCs give you!
I think I've said enough.  It goes without saying that every audiophile should have this in his or her Steam library.  If you don't, you are missing out on a totally innovative musical experience!

FTL is one of those games that I don't know whether to love or hate. On the one hand, FTL is a magnificent game that provides tons of enjoyment and thus opportunity for many hours of enjoyment. On the other hand, once you pierce the surface you are not entirely sure what is left to keep you coming back: despite a plethora of options in terms of upgrades, weapons, drones, and crewmembers, after a while the selection seems less substantial than initial appearances. This appearance can change once you unlock more ships and ship layouts, but the task of unlocking these are overly complicated. In order to unlock ships and/or their layouts you need to complete tasks or beat "the game". The game is essentially the same concept: you must move through a series of sectors without being destroyed (either through crew death or ship explosion, although the latter certainly entails the former) until you reach the final sector and destroy the rebel "mothership": if there is more than that I could not tell you, for this task alone I have not been able to complete.
Why is the task so difficult? This can be seen partially out of skill: if you are not fighting properly or not upgrading your ship sufficientily you will be hard pressed to make it past the first 3 sectors. Yet even moreso it seems to be largely based on luck. You can find yourself really well off only to be completely annihilated on the next node for little more than what pops up and one selection you make. The harder the difficulty (even "easy" is not all that easy, at least not for many hours of practice and patience) the more likely your choices will provide negative results. For instance: you can come across a civilian crew in need help of this or that task. Sometimes you will have a unique solution to said task depending on your crew members (certain races have certain advantages/disadvantages), and in this case the outcome is almost always positive. Yet where such options are not present you can find yourself in a tough situation: you can help them and potentially gain a reward, or help them and lose a crew member or some other such unfortunate event. But if you never help civilians and never try your luck, you wind up with no resources to upgrade your ship and will be destroyed after a few sectors.
This creates a sort of "damned if you do, damned if you don't" feeling to the game. I have played this game practically non-stop since I have gotten it, I have gotten slightly better and learned more how to handle my ship and crew. Yet regardless of how well I have been improving, the "luck" aspect of the game seems to rule all: whether it be the consequences of your actions or even just a simple layout of a sector and the nodes within it you can quickly find yourself doomed regardless of how prepped your ship is. I have found myself armed to the teeth with nice weapons and shields only to be destroyed the next node do to some unforeseen environmental hazard or some unexpectedly powerful pirate ship.
So why do I still insist on recommending this game if I seem to have so many contentions with it? The answer is simple: because despite its challenges and infuriating random encounters that make or break your next move (and every move after), the game still manages to sucker you back in to keep playing it. You want to have that breakthrough, you want to have that moment of &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥yeah! I just wiped out an entire rebel fleet single-handedly!" Having said that, if you are not into diligently playing a game in order to master it, then this game certainly is not for you. But for those who admire a challenge and don't mind getting some life-force sucked out of them for many hours, there is perhaps no better game out there.
This game has the same infuriating charm as old platformers like Castlevania did (and still do): you want to learn the moves and master the castle. Yet unlike some of those old platformers, this game seems to create some new phenomenon in that there is no "move". Levels aren't one based on muscle-memory of when to press this or that button, but on an overall understanding of the situation and tried and true methods of dealing with said situation.
Is the game perfect? No. Is the game as customizable as it may seem? For me it wasn't, but that doesn't take away from its charm. Is the game worth playing? If you can deal with everything I have mentioned, then it is more than worth playing. Is there a reason why this review is so damn long? Probably, but I haven't talked with the proper professionals to figure that one out.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a turn-based tactical RPG, which can be played in single-player campaign mode or in multiplayer mode. Released in 2012 and using the UE3 Engine, Enemy Unknown takes place in a future where aliens have invaded earth and you are the last line of defense. As the commander, you direct soldiers turn-based style to eliminate alien threats, secure objectives, and more. At the end of each mission, prior to the start of the next, you have the ability to use do research, and create new technologies, as well as handle your finances.
Visually, I think the game looks pretty good for being 3 years old. The fog of war is well done, and there are multiple difficulty settings to give players even more of a challenge. I played on Impossible mode, as well as Ironman mode, with all the special features turned on to make the game as challenging as possible and it worked. The AI is great and can present a challenge to those who rush in, forcing you to actually use tactics to clear objectives. Enemy Unknown also has an expansion called, XCOM: Enemy Within, which adds a variety of content. The Elite Edition contains all DLC Content and is the best deal if you are interested in picking up this game. I'm not a huge fan of turn-based gameplay, but this is actually a really great game, nicely done, and worth paying for.

An overall decent Texas Hold'em simulator, but the real stars here are your opponents, seeming almost randomly selected based on their backgrounds: Max from the Sam & Max franchise, Strongbad of Homestar Runner, The Heavy from Team Fortress 2, and Tycho of Penny Arcade. Telltale Games has outdone themselves creating an immersive experience with these third party characters, matching their personality to a T when it comes to dialogue and interactions: Max tells stories about fighting crime with Sam, Strongbad rants and raves just like with his email videos, Heavy thinks of the chips as his 'team' and blames the Spy whenever he gets a bad hand, and Tycho makes various different tabletop, card, and video game references. They play the game exactly like you would expect them to, which is a great feat in itself considering the licensing TTG must have had to go through. Even though Poker Night 2 is on the horizon and to be released this month, the original should not be overlooked. There are still special crossover TF2 items to be unlocked, and you won't be seeing any of the original cast (aside from cameos by Max) in the sequel. Definitely worth the buy.

Being a fan of the Game of Thrones series, it was easy for me to get into this game quick. You play as members of a family not really talked about in the show, but still you feel as if your family has an integral part in the Game of Thrones. You bounce around from your lands in north Westeros to lands in across the narrow sea and even Kings Landing. You play as multiple members of this family as they struggle to remain relevant when they lost almost everything because they were allied with the Starks during the famous red wedding. If you are into Game of Thrones and story driven games you may enjoy this. It has that Game of Thrones feeling where anyone can die no matter how important they are at any point and it just keeps that suspense alive. Although, having played this game twice now, doing a playthrough with the complete opposite choices I picked the first time, I can say that 95% of your choices mean nothing, the same outcome either way, just minor picks as to who the lord is thats alive at the end, and who ends up betraying your house. I am annoyed. I give this game a 5 out of 10 and I hope to see Telltale follow up with a more redeeming second season for their Game of Thrones title.

While not as strong as previous Telltale titles, Game of Thrones is still a worthy addition to their repitoir of point-and-click episodic adventures. While not personally a Game of Thrones fan, I still managed to find the story reasonabley immersive, and most of the characters interesting. However, I do feel that Telltale were over-ambitious in setting up four protagonists to play as. While Gared, Rodrick, Asher and Mira all have the over-arching quest to save house Forrester, I definately found the latter two had much weaker personal storylines than the former. That's not to say I didn't like the characters, but Asher and Mira's storylines, to me, were by far the worst written and the least interesting. Therefore I didn't feel as invested in Game of Thrones' story to the same extent as I did in other Telltale games, most notabley The Walking Dead and Tales From the Borderlands. Perhaps this is also due to the fact the game didn't seem to have the same heart as those previous titles either. Hyperdimension Neptunia Rebirth 1 is a JRPG that tries not to take itself too seriously, nyu.
There are many recurring jokes and gags revolving around, but not limited to:
+ Mispronouncing names, it’s Broccoli nyu.
+ Breast size
+ Pudding
+ Lesbian undertones
+ Loners
+ Gamers
The game itself is a bit kiddish with minor amounts of fan service.  Things are pretty tame, but there are plenty of breasts. Dare I say the game might even be a little girly.
The combat system is complex enough to be interesting while generally being easy enough to figure out.
The last 3rd of the game or so becomes relatively easy. The first half of the game or so has some major balance issues. Often times you could find yourself stomping through an area with little effort and then getting to a boss fight and getting 1 hit from 75% health. This will probably force you to grind at least a little bit. You will do this frequently until towards the end, not knowing if you are strong enough to fight a boss.
The story is nothing really special. There is a lot of content reuse.  Most dungeons are clones of one another.
Like a recent game I played called Tales of Zestiria, it must be a JRPG thing, to have the worst camera controls ever. Although not as bad as Zestiria, worth a mention.
You will spend the majority of the game with the same general characters, but toward the end of the game you are bombarded with new, and arguably useless characters. Although some of the characters are cool, there just doesn’t feel like a need to even have them in the game at the point. Most of them don’t do anything that different or better than the ones you have and the back-story for them are generally completely missing.
The game does a good job of not really wasting your time other than forcing you to grind a little bit. How much extra you explore, how many extra ingredients you get, item upgrades, etc.. don’t really seem to matter as much. If you really want you could probably spend 60+ hours on one play through, but you don’t have to.
The voice work is not bad, but I wouldn’t say it’s fantastic.
Overall the characters are just good enough, and the game play passable enough that the game is enjoyable enough I would say go play it. It won’t win any awards but it’s not a bad game by any stretch of the imagination.

As said already, the mechanics of the game are good.  Has a nice cover system and a lot of eye-candy.  They still kept the turn-based aspect of the game, which I have always enjoyed.  Now, here comes what I was disappointed by.  The game feels too linear.  They seem to have an event system which from game to game, is always the same.  In the old games, you simply had random ecounters/raids and would have random enemies.  X-COM: Enemy Unknown progresses too linear without as many surprises.
Secondly, what I hated most about this game, is that they removed the base building and management.  In the old games, you could have 5 or 6 (or more) bases setup across the world, wherever you deployed them (assuming you could afford building), and you could set them up as many things... item stashes, training facilities, radar scanning bases, troop launch sites, etc.  You would also need to mange your finances to add onto these facilities.  Not only were you fighting, but you had the base building and financial management in the game as well.  It was more sandbox and allowed for more various gameplay types.  X-COM: Enemy Unknown is one of those newer 'hand-holding' games... not as much freedom.
So, the game revamped... graphically, it's good.  Mechanically, it's good.  Features wise, I feel it is lacking.  It is partly faithful to the original games, with elements missing.  It was enjoyable to play, but didn't get nearly as much replayability from it as I have from X-COM: UFO Defense/X-COM: Terror from the Deep.

I have never played a Tropico game before, but I love city builders. Pharoah, Caeser, Simcity... love 'em all. I became interested in this game after hearing it called a Banana Republic simulator, so I picked it up in a sale.
The game is solid, I'll give you that. It captures the essential elements that make a city game classic - macro and micromanagement. The choices are there, simple as they are, and it adds a good layer of complexity to the game.
The game suffers from severe traffic problems, and larger cities are tough to have because traffic becomes hellish. Building a large island in general seems to be very very tough. I could make a bunch of money, but I couldn't get my people to not drive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
The campaign is fun, but jumps randomly in difficulty. Sandbox is fun. This game is totally worth it in a sale. I have not touched any of the DLC, though, so I don't know about it. I've heard Modern Times is unbalanced.
edit: Fun fact! This was one of my first reviews after Valve changed how reviews work. They used to be limited to something like 250 characters!
Anyway, years later, I've put in a respectable amount of time with this game, and also obtained the complete DLC collection and played a good number maps with them.
Speaking to the overall longevity of the game, I found the campaign missions to get a bit repetitive after awhile. I finished around half of them and never returned, instead opting to cycle through many sandbox games with a variety of options ticked. I found the Sandbox mode more satisfying overall, and a big part of the reason why is that the late game of Tropico is more fun to manage than the early stage, in my opinion. Early on, the game involves a lot of debt and waiting for freighters to pick up your exports. Late game, you're a dictation-machine building a Banana Republic that would make any cartoon communist proud.
The DLC is interesting; some of the buildings make me feel like I'm cheating, but the more I play, the more they feel like they aren't as much cheating as they are filling some serious holes the game has in creative ways. Some of the buildings in Tropico didn't scale well, and most of the DLC aims to give you functional buildings with higher capacities that run more efficient, in order to help aid in the construction of big cities.
The Modern Times expansion really fills in a ton of holes in late game Tropico - late game gridlock can be solved with some quick tranist stations, for example. It makes the game much more fun, and as at this point the game goes on sale often enough for cheap, I must heartily endorse the DLC as a valuable investment. It helps make some frustrating aspects of the game less so, and helps you focus on making your utopia of dictorships.
Tropico 4 is a great city builder, and worthy of a pickup along with the DLC. It integrates rather seamlessly into the game, and will just make it a more enjoyable experience overall.

Dying Light is everything Dead Island should have been and more.
But, in the interest of fairness, I will list pros AND cons I've noticed during my playtime.
Pros:
-stunning graphics even on medium settings
-excellent sound design (horrific zombie noises, immersive ambient sound, you name it!)
-fluid parkour mechanics/gameplay (think Mirror's Edge meets Assassin's Creed)
-innovative "Day/Night" mechanic (seriously, night time is straight up terrifying)
-realistic combat (melee is brutal, guns are most effective with headshots, explosives aren't OP)
-seamless multiplayer co-op (drop in, drop out, never miss a beat)
-tons of interesting side quests (they often follow a formula but rarely feel repetitive)
-BADASS crafting system (and it's easy to master)
-scavenging for supplies makes the environment more fun to explore
-hands down one of THE BEST DLCs I have ever played (SPIKEY, FLAMETHROWERY DEATH BUGGY OF DOOM)
Cons:
-enemy AI can be a bit OP at times (near perfect aim, the dreaded "over-head tracking", seeing through walls)
[I'm looking at YOU Virals!]
-Main Story is a bit cliche
-Characters lack backstory and rarely undergo growth (yet we are expected to "care" about them)
-the main game is a bit short (but to be fair, the DLC is kickass and extends gameplay significantly)
-once you hit max level you can pretty much one shot anything (not as scary anymore)
-Night Hunter PvP mode is a hot mess at best, a complete joke at worst
-not as many people playing anymore, so it can be difficult to find co-op partners
-the ending (of both the main game, and DLC) is a bit.... lackluster
BUGS ABOUND! But they don't take away from the game in any way (at least not in my experience).
I found most of them to be amusing.
To summarize my thoughts on this game:
Buy it.
It's absolutely worth playing for the parkour element alone.
The beginning is difficult (especially on hard mode, which I prefer and recommend) but please stick with it!
You'll find yourself wondering where the hours have gone, it really is that much fun.
SOLID 8/10

In Double Action you choose from one of 4 preset characters (One somehow Nick from Left 4 Dead 2) select 2 weapons for your loadout, and then duke it out in a free-for-all against a ton of other players. The scoring system is based on "style points" you get those by doing trickshots and stunts like diving, flipping, sliding, slowing down time, etc. The person with the highest style points wins the match. Also a neat feature is the ability to switch between first-person and third-person view modes, although third person really feels best. There's only a handful of maps at the moment, and the matches sometimes feel like they drag on forever, but it's pretty fun for a free game.
+ It's completely free, no microtransaction ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t
+ Is very fun in small bursts
+ Max payne anyone?
+ Specs are low enough for older machines

Then I remembered I have this program Cortex by Razer that can boost game performance and while it never did much on my old PC, what a difference it made this time! I was gettingabout 30-50fps on ultra, lower a few things like shadows to high (which I think look better anyways being less sharp and more soft and realistic) and geometry to high and I was getting 45-60fps usually around 50. Now on ultra don't get lower than 60 and up to 90 and if I lower only shadows to my prefered high setting I get 80-104. I do still get stuttering occasionally but not nearly as often and it isn't taking away from the game. Funny though the game doesn't seem to be any less "laggy" or smoother with the increased fps. Runs just like it did when I first started playing. Had a stupid troll debating fps and expensive hardware like his opinion matters regarding my enjoyment and performance of a game. Anyways. CPU - FX 8320 3.5-4GHz 8 core

Original: I think this game is great. I have had no issues so far. I see lots of people with high end GPUs and SLI/Crossfire are having issues. Sucks to have spent that much money on hardware and not have it perform much better than the mid grade stuff. I See that all the time. I have a GTX 960 and I have no issues running ultra with shadows on high at 1920x1080p. I may not be getting 60fps all the time, or even often, but over 40 is good enough. Usually I get around 50fps. FarCry game where you hunt, gather, craft, kill, and do missions and run errands...WOW what a surprise. I have read a lot of people saying it is reptitive. You hunt and gather and kill people and run errands and build up your village. Well what the heck were you expecting? How is that really much different from any open world game ever made? It is even advertised to be that kind of game in a franchise that is based on that type of gameplay.
So far I find the story to be good. The characters are interesting (I still have many to meet). The hunting is interesting, some thing I expected to be a bit scarier, like the bears and a pack of wolves but so far not really. The mammoths are quite a challange though. Night time is a bit harder, especially if your brightness and gamma settings are a bit lower. I have enjoyed exploring the rocky forests near the begining of the game. I can see playing this game for quite a while.
The only cons I can think of so far are:
1) that there isn't a separate volume control for the music from the master volume. Some times the music is louder than I would like. I never like music over powering the ambient sounds in a game, especially this type of game. But it doesn't happen when I actually need to hear.
2) there is a filmgrain filter that cannot be turned off (maybe with a mod?). I mostly only notice it in darker areas but it makes things look fuzzy.
Also does not look quite as good as in the screen shots. The AA could be better and some time textures seem a bit lower than others, like some rocks with moss for example.
Regardless though, the game is still quite immersive.
There are lots of good settings like turning of all indicators to make the game more realistic. The graphics are pretty great, although I do recall FarCry 4 looking a bit better. The map is pretty huge. At first I thought it seemed a bit smaller but after running around for 3 hours I discovered I really haven't explored as much as I thought. I find the primative weapons to be quite fun to work with. I think of this as a full FarCry stand alone game, not at all like Blood Dragon but more like the main games. Not sure why people think of it as a spin off. None of the games are realated in any way except gameplay anyways. this game could of been called FarCry 5 Primal but like in the AC franchise after 4 they stopped using numbers and I don't recall people reffering to Rouge, Unity or Syndicate as spin offs.
Anyways, I totally recomend this game. I am happy I got it and am happy I can play it.
For those of you who are actually have troubles launching the game or experiencing crashes, I hope there is a soulution found soon for you.

Great to see classic RTS made in such great quality! All what we love in RTS from the past is here: base building, troops training without any cap, resource collecting - all that is so refreshing now, compared to "new innovative casual RTS". It's been so long, since we all could play a PROPER RTS game!!!
What impressed me most - is how it is friendly to newcomers to both RTS genre as a whole and to standard RTS we played in the past:
- great single player campaign with very very nice quality CGI cut-scenes lets you get used to all mechanics gradually
- don't want to wait and learn by practice? GREATEST way to handle complete newcomers: very detailed encyclopedia: will teach you how to play RTS as a whole (have 8 minutes video lesson with lots of useful hints), if it is your firts game of this genre.
- veteran of RTS? Only interested in multiplayer? But need to know what units are about? Complete tech tree with all units, structures and upgrades, with stats, decruptions and balance. Spend some time reading and here you go - jump into multiplayer
- tools for creating your own maps and campaigns. Want to surprise the world with your story and missions? Create and share them. Play in maps other players create.
So the way how game handles both veterans and complete newcomers is amazing. That for me is some kind of standard now, how it should be done in any other next strategy game.
The factions are nice, Goo faction is very interesting to explore and see how it plays. So if you want the classic experience from Command and Conquer original games, with some new gameplay mechanics, you definetely will found yourself spent into the game lots of hours :) I'm sure this game has great potential and future ahead.
And once again thanks a lot to Steam for having such free weekends when we can find and try such interesting games!

I've been putting off getting this one for quite some time, and being the frugal gamer that I am, I was happy to be able to pick it up in a recent Humble Bundle, along with Legend of Grimrock 2 and some awesome Zachtronics titles, for just $14.
Crate really did something great with this game here. As you can see, I've owned it less than a week and have already sunk a massive chunk of time into it. If you like ARPG's like Diablo and Path of Exile, you do not want to pass this one up.
I LOVE the setting of this game. I'm kind of a sucker for steampunky dark fantasy in the first place, but Crate excells at every moment in their creation of this dark and gritty world where♥♥♥♥♥♥s so bleak, they use iron for currency. Parts of the setting remind me of the Warhammer universe during the End Times. Frankly, I just don't think I could state enough how ♥♥♥♥ing \m/ metal \m/ this world is.
I also really like the amount of customization for your character. It doesn't get super crazy like PoE with the huge skill tree that you need three monitors to even be able to view the whole thing. Each mastery does have 25 unique skills and spells to choose from though, and at level 10 you are able to pick up a second mastery, effectively raising the number of classes in the game to 21, making for some pretty awesome combos (like Occultist + Demolitionist = Pyromancer). Not to mention, with the included mod tools, you can create your own class from scratch and add synergies to other game assets, or just take advantage of the amazing mod community and add some of their work to your game to make things more interesting.
And speaking of mods, fans of Crate's previous game Titan Quest may remember the excellent Xmax mod. Well it's back in Grim Dawn! Just search the mod communities for Grimmest Dawn and you're sure to find it!
Dark fantasy done right. Crate really hit one out of the park with this game. Still plenty of support and further development going into the game as well. Next time you see this game for half off or part of some ridiculous pay what you want bundle, you better make sure you pick it up.

This is stuck between the two best star wars games ever made, the other being of course knights of the old republic. The gameplay is fluid and fun, the choice between third and first person makes the game easily adaptable to any shooter fan. Although it has aged since 2005 it surely is still a great game. Unfortuneatly as GameSpy shut down, the multiplayer has become unavailable but you can still play against bots in instant action, galactic conquest or the single player campaign. This brings me to my next point, the galactic conquest mode, it is very enjoyable as it brings a strategic style to the game and prevents you from getting bored of playing the same maps over and over again. The game is highly moddable, allowing for new maps, characters and game modes which allows the game to still have the same level of fun as when it was first released.
The single player campaign follows various soldiers of the 501st legion, also known as "vader's fist", as you fight to conquer the galaxy and closely follows the 3rd prequel to the star wars films. the story is relatively well written but what makes the campaign different to the other game modes is that you will be given specific objectives throughout the map, for example you will be told to attack or defend a certain station, or destroy a vehicle etc.
This game is a definite must play and I highly reccomend that you pay the US $10 for this game as it holds many good times and can be friendly to kids and adults of all ages. It is definitely a treasure among the star wars expanded universe media and one of the best games ever made in my opinion.
Also if you are a fan of the battlefield series this game would be very good for you as many game modes and such are remniscient of the series

Since the announcment of Battlefront 3, I decided to rebuy Battlefront 2 on Steam because I previously owned it on the Playstation 2. Since then I've been having a blast with this game.
The PC version if it is for sure the best version out there (like most games PC master race) I find the visuals to be extremely good for the time aswell. It's hard to review a game that's almost ten years old now, but I still feel like no matter what, every game has it's flaws.
I personally prefer playing games in first person rather than third person, luckily, this game has the option to switch between them during combat just by pressing the V key or by changing the setting in the options. The animation quality in third person is absolutly amazing and feels real, although the animation quality when playing in first person really lacks. It just seems boring to play in first person with this game. The game's AI system is also whack. I'm pointing this out because the multiplayer servers are down so you're basically limited just to single player.
That's basically it for the complaints. The stuff I really love about this game though involves the map layout, concept, and the gameplay. It lacks a good story but wins at the gameplay most of all. You get an amazing rush through your body while sprinting into a battle as a Clone trooper while lazers shoot at all angles while hearing screams, droid chatter, and explosions. Or not to mention flying through space while ships spin out around you, just for you to single handedly board a ship and destroy it. Not to mention playing as a Jedi or Sith, tearing through droids, rebels, and clones. Each time you play a map it always feels different, you can flank from different routes or play through it as a different type of class.
Overall, this game is worth the buy, and certainly is still not outdated.

This game isn't bad, it just could be much better.

You HAVE to have a decent class line-up otherwise it's almost impossible to play.
I'll come back in a year or two and edit my review then, but as for now I'd advise players to wait a little while on this one.
It's a great idea, being able to have total control in a team based shooter, it just needs time to refine it.
This game is filled with ideas that look great on paper, but when you put in motion it all falls apart.
Tony (This game's version of the engineer) is painfully weak. He has a rivet gun (Shot-gun) but the damn thing is extremely inaccurate and when you do hit, everyone completely out damages you almost instantly. He can place seven sentries, but none of them are any good. They all have a painfully small health pool and do almost nothing for damage against everyone other than another tony.
Defending is much harder for the simple fact that they always tunnel in on the cube (What you must protect) completely bypassing the tony's sad excuse for a defense. what you end up with because of this is a messy cesspool riddled with holes of variours depths and tunnels going 9,0000 different ways, which makes defense all but impossible because without spending a good portion of the round smoothing the area around the cube out, there's no point behind placing sentries or traps or anything else for that matter. If they were to removed the digging aspect when near cubes, that would be fine.
(I like the buliding aspect, not a huge fan of the digging. it's annoying to deal with.)
This game's version of the spy, while very strong (He's an infiltrator with a small health pool, if he's not dealing hefty damage, there's no point behind having him) at times feels too strong. that's manily because he "teleport" anywhere on the map with ease and the moment he takes too much damage he can just "Teleport" out of harms way.
Nigel, this games version of the sniper, is... okay? he can head-shot (For a lot of damage, but I don't think it flat-out kills someone) is odd in the sense that he has no-scope, making longer range marksmenship nearly pointless (A sniper that can't snipe all that well, Sounds really stupid but hey.) which leads to him being played more as a CQC class, which because his rifle has no scope, he does quite well with.
In TF2 you can phase into and out of players on your own team, in this game it's the reverse. You can't phase out of your own team( Is a utter nightmare when a newer player follows you down a hole and you want to go out the way you came in.) but you can phase into and past the enemy team, which makes CQC at times literally spray and pray. (Most likely why Tony's Shot-gun is utterly worthless, which it is. It's something even the "Vets" mostly agree on. it's too weak and too inaccurate to be his sole means of self defense.)
Tony can buff his sentries (At a cost of chewing through his ammo) to deal arguably greater damage, which is fantasic on paper because of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ his sentries are on their own. However, you have no idea when your sentries firing on someone or being fired on when you have seven of them scattered across the map. you can repair them also while someones firing on them, but the range of his repair tool is sad. you tend to take spash damage when a cog or sarge is spamming at it, but most of the time it's pointless to even bother fighting off cogs/sarges due to their higher health and greater damage out-put. even if you can catch one low on health, you'll most likely still lose due to how lack-luster the rivet gun is.
Tony can not place respawn pads, which is odd because that would give him a greater offense role. (Setting up forward bases would be much easier.)
The respawn rate is... Bad would be a compliment. (34 seconds... Just let that sink in for a moment. Thought 20 seconds was bad, I feel sorry for you.)
Map sizes are quite nice though, would prefer if each side got seven players, but five is alright.
Sarge (This games version of the soldier) is pretty worthless all and all. Because a tony can place health and ammo packs, Sarge can't. If you haven't unlocked Cog yet he's okay in a very loose way. But the moment you get a cog, do not bother with Sarge. Everything Sarge does, cog literally does 10X better.
All of this aside, the game can be something that can go toe-toe with TF2, just not right now. A few years time, this game might be something truly good.

Dying Light is everything Dead Island should have been and more.
But, in the interest of fairness, I will list pros AND cons I've noticed during my playtime.
Pros:
-stunning graphics even on medium settings
-excellent sound design (horrific zombie noises, immersive ambient sound, you name it!)
-fluid parkour mechanics/gameplay (think Mirror's Edge meets Assassin's Creed)
-innovative "Day/Night" mechanic (seriously, night time is straight up terrifying)
-realistic combat (melee is brutal, guns are most effective with headshots, explosives aren't OP)
-seamless multiplayer co-op (drop in, drop out, never miss a beat)
-tons of interesting side quests (they often follow a formula but rarely feel repetitive)
-BADASS crafting system (and it's easy to master)
-scavenging for supplies makes the environment more fun to explore
-hands down one of THE BEST DLCs I have ever played (SPIKEY, FLAMETHROWERY DEATH BUGGY OF DOOM)
Cons:
-enemy AI can be a bit OP at times (near perfect aim, the dreaded "over-head tracking", seeing through walls)
[I'm looking at YOU Virals!]
-Main Story is a bit cliche
-Characters lack backstory and rarely undergo growth (yet we are expected to "care" about them)
-the main game is a bit short (but to be fair, the DLC is kickass and extends gameplay significantly)
-once you hit max level you can pretty much one shot anything (not as scary anymore)
-Night Hunter PvP mode is a hot mess at best, a complete joke at worst
-not as many people playing anymore, so it can be difficult to find co-op partners
-the ending (of both the main game, and DLC) is a bit.... lackluster
BUGS ABOUND! But they don't take away from the game in any way (at least not in my experience).
I found most of them to be amusing.
To summarize my thoughts on this game:
Buy it.
It's absolutely worth playing for the parkour element alone.
The beginning is difficult (especially on hard mode, which I prefer and recommend) but please stick with it!
You'll find yourself wondering where the hours have gone, it really is that much fun.
SOLID 8/10

This backroom Poker tournament simulator of sorts is one of those games that I wouldn't have expected to grow quite so much on me. Granted, playing Poker against artificial intelligence doesn't entail the same satisfaction that one gets from successfully bluffing or showing a superior hand to fellow human players, however the entertainment value here lies within the often satirical, tongue-in-cheek and cleverly crass character dialogue and interactions with one another, complimented by the appropriately ambient visuals and music. To enjoy the spoken content at its best, be sure to enable maximum chatter in the options menu. I personally relish the sense of humor in this game, and will sometimes just sit idly at the virtual table simply watching and listening to the banter going back and forth; from Heavy's uncharacteristically tender and touching anecdote of a sparrow encountered back at Motherland, to Tycho's eyebrow-raising fantasies of intimately bonding with particular species of animals.
When set to Easy, this game offers a fun way for players who are new to the Texas Hold 'em variant of Poker to grasp its fundamentals, however in order to get proper practice it's ultimately best to experience playing against real people with their own individual tactical mindsets as opposed to fictional characters with preset and non-unique betting behaviors.

I felt like I had to make this review, because this game is amazing. I know that my Steam hours may not show it, but this game changed me, I look at things differently now.
Characters - Alot of people comment on the poor voice acting and unlikeable characters. I loved the characters, they had decent backstory and they didn't feel shoved in, they really were just trying to survive. Kyle Crane is a sarcastic, typical hero, he does what he has to but tends to have a good grumble along the way and he is charismatic, in some strange way.
General Gameplay - The gameplay is *SO* fun, it's amazing just running around and lopping off the body parts of zombies, whom after a while you start to feel sorry for, because of their plain defenselessness, which does create an issue where you are incredibly overpowered, a problem which was fixed by the introduction of hard and nightmare mode. Also, the AI changes made in the Following DLC were very clear to see, zombies were made much more aggresive, which made the game much more difficult and also much more exhilirating. The buggy is awesome, honestly I don't think that I got into it as much as others, but coming from someone who hates racing games with a passion, the buggy mechanics are smooth and feel realistic yet also very fun.
Main story - The story in general is actually very interesting, it introduces you to some rather strange characters who have managed to survive through alot of the apocalypse. Rais definetly reminded me of Vaas from Far Cry 3, in that he was a man who was evidently more inteligent than the others around him, but also more brutal and understood what needed to be done to stay at the top of the food chain.
Side Quests - I think the side quests deserve their own paragraph, just to make clear how amazing they are. I mean holy crap, some of them are VERY long, but all of them are interesting, they all showcase even more of the city (and countryside I guess :D) of the city of Harran and it's seemingly numerous deranged inhabitants (seriously, how did it end up that most of the people with mental disorders of some kind have survived for the longest?) , which just allows for even more amazing and bizarre quests.
The Following - I've mentioned the Following briefly, so just to finish up this review I wanted to state that the buggy system is very cool, I love all the new quests and side quests added and the trust system is interesting and I would like to see it again (Possibly a future DLC involving it again?) and I enjoyed the many changed to game mechanics and AI, along with the addition of many new weapons and outfits.
Conclusion - In conclusion, this game is awesome and if you actually think about what is going on instead of just running around hacking and slashing, this game will become even more amazing, because of the profound effects it can have (At least on me :P). I am really, really hoping for more DLC and a sequel at some point, because I loved this game so much and the ending to the base game and the Following set it up perfectly for even more content.
Thank you for reading this huge wall of text, if you enjoyed it then please consider saying that this was helpful, as I sit here writing this at five o'clock in the morning.

Well, there's a certain humor to the Divinity games, not everyone might get.
They simply don't take themselves serious, but there is more behind it, than cheap laughs.
As a fan of top-down RPGs and Divine/Beyond Divinity it was clear that I had to play this game. In my opinion it takes all the good stuff from the old games and adds a few more.
I adore the system of elements and status effects. Throw an oil barrel in a hoard of zombies with your telekinesis ability, then ignite it with some fire attack, shoot them with your arrows and their acid blood will cause more damaging explosions and burns. Stun the bandit leader in the puddle of his gangmember's blood. Whatever you like! It really is awesome and a lot of fun to explore the different effects.
The difficulty is quite high, especially at the beginning, but luckily for us there is a quicksave button. I love a good and fair challenge and I never felt as if the game was really unfair until now. It is unforgiving, though :)
The story so far is nothing to complain about, it's mainly high fantasy with a few twists and a specific wit. It's kind of like a loving parody on very serious fantasy RPGs, but not too ridiculous.
The multiplayer works pretty well and my buddo and I still have a ton of fun playing through the campaign.
There's just so much to explore and uncover, I simply love it.
Probably 9,5/10 for me :)

Later on, your pilots are flying the Firestorm, highly advanced fighter ship which is more or less alien in origin, and can be equipped with such awesome firepower as the plasma cannon, or the fusion lance.

So, what are you waiting for? Go kick some alien butt.

Imagine Super Smash Bros crossed with tennis and you've got Lethal League. A fighting game in spirit, Lethal League pits you and 1-3 more players in an arena with a ball. A single, deadly ball. The objective is quite simple, hit the ball and cause it to strike your foes, killing them instantly. The controls, much like the concept are simple with only three main functions: swing, bunt and jump, with directional modifiers included for swings. You've got several modes at your disposal, with the default mode being Free for All Stock matches, wherein it's every man for himself trying to eliminate the competition until they are the only one with any stocks remaining (this one is my personal favorite). Other modes include Teams (self-explanatory) and Strikers, where you're invincible and have to hit the opposing team's goal with the ball to score. Finally, this game has awesome netcode and is extremely playable even with ~110 ping, so even people as remote as myself can enjoy it. There's also decent bots for solo players, if local multiplayer isn't an option and online isn't your thing. All in all, a very fun game.

FTL is rad rouge-like-like which presents you with battle and narrative scenarios which one might liken to Star Trek. A Rebellion armada is conquering the galaxy and only the sensitive inforamtion you carry aboard your ship can turn the tide of battle in favor of The Federation. FTL is broken up into a couple of different systems that provide hours of fun and experimentation. Upgrade your ship by collecting scrap from battle or from different types of encounters. Then spend that scrap on your ship systems like shields, weapons, life support, or even better doors. The combat system fits incredibly well with the theme and makes a vairety of strategies vialble for success. For example, you can use missle type weapons that by pass shileds, laser weapons that have infinte ammunition, ion cannons that disrupt systems without doing damage, automated bots that chip at enemey shileds, teleporters for boarding ships, or any combination of the previoulsy mentioned.
On top of the great mechanics, FTL provides narrative choices that are so much more than basic black and white morality calls. Do you want your crew to investigate a mysterious derlict ship or should they blow it up and collect the valuable leftover scrap? Slavers with supeiror fire power have cornered you and are demanding you turn over one of your crew members in order for you to continue unharmed. It's up to you wether or not you send that crew member to his fate or stand up to the pirates, all while the balance of the galaxy rests on your shoulders.
Customize and command your ship throughout the cosmos, meet all sorts of new alien races, and experience all the cool nuances of this awesome world created by Subset Games - you won't regret it! Play FTL: Faster Than Light!

Apart from the RNG cesspool and the Alienware circle jerk/rant parties In chat, Black Desert has a lot to offer. After a month of playing this game with 250 hours of my life stripped from me, I'm writing this review with two level 56 classes, a few hours invested into life skill and a Gear score of 330 which is mediocre at best.
There are currently 14 classes in the game that fit any playstyle imaginable. When the game starts you wake up with your chosen class having "lost" your memories. Following this inconvenience, you're prompted to learn your class skills and explore the starting area for the first few hours. I recommended to follow the main quest line for your first character since it gives inventory spaces and contribution points which will come in handy later in the game. Through out your first days of Black Desert you will be spoonfed money and gear and it might delude some into thinking they're set for life, suprise! you're not. After a few weeks of exploring and questing you would eventually hit level 56, this is where everything is about to change. Rookie rewards end, gear upgrades become more expensive and tedious and you'll have to figure out ways to obtain money by yourself. On the bright side, you become "awakened" which is essentially your character getting his/her memories back. You unlock a new set of skills and a new weapon which is a welcomed breath of refreshment after hours of spamming the same abilities.
- Fluid combat system
- Dynamic weather and day/night cycle
- Beautiful environment
- In depth life skills
- Steady character progression
- Detailed character customization
- Simple yet detailed worker mechanics
-
- Large scale Guild vs Guild battles
------------------------------------
- No fast travel (makes the game immersive but also inconvenient)
------------------------------------
- Heavy microtransactions

Servers are a lot better now as of 6/29
- RNG everything.
- Gender locked characters.
Black Desert Online Is a MMO that treads away from some of the unwritten laws of a generic MMO. Gear progression and No fast travel are just some of the things that make Black Desert unique in my eyes. Black Desert is a game everyone can enjoy whether they prefer active online PvPing or just casual life skilling, and yes it is possible to get good at the game without obtaining a neckbeard.

[WARNING]
NOT FOR PEOPLE WITH EPILEPSY CONDITIONS NOR THOSE SENSITIVE TO STROBBING AND FLASHING LIGHTS! WHILE YOU CAN REDUCE THE INTENSITY IN THE SETTINGS IT IS STILL WAY LARGER THAN THE NORMAL AMOUNT!
[WARNING]
TL;DR: Spaceship, meets star arena meet asteroid with your music providing the tempo for the weapons and enemies! Enjoyable for those who like to challenge themselves since the INSANE difficiulity is definitely insane!
Review Starts Here
What is Beat Hazard?
Beat hazard is a 2D top down space shooter game in the veins of asteroid except you have enemies and boss fights. Pretty darn awesome. You have to supply it with your music though.
1:Graphics
Notice the [WARNING] thing above? well not kidding. Each effects is the same as a single flashbang and every shots and explosion from either you or the enemy will sear the screen as bright as the sun causing temperorary blindness and mania in the affected gamers. God forbid you crank up the effect to 200% like i did and played for 30 min straight.
The actual graphics themselves are very good as far as 2D spaceshooting game is concern. Sprite move, shoot and explode brilliantly when they die. Meanwhile the 3D effects zoom across the screen blinding you with their colourful effects. And they are bright.
2: Sound
Shooting sounds good, explosive sounds good.
For anything else music, you supply it yourself.
3:Gameplay
You get 2 meter, power and volume meter, collecting powerup increases either the bar game which in turn either increases your shot power or shot intensity respectively. Mostly you want the intensity though because depending on the music the AI can really prove to be a challenge with them swarming you on all side so breaking through will definitely help more.
At the start of the game you are provided with 3 bombs that clear HALF the map of enemies and not the whole map. If you die a bomb would automatically be used should one be in your possesion.
Perks can be purchase with cash you collect as you destroy craft but only a limited number can be activated at time, they provide in game benefits when you activate them.
As you play along the game sometimes boss can appear, these hulking monstrosity often has a gimmick behind thier sleeves that can prove to be rather challenging if you are terrible with them but killing them often provides money and powerups.
The game will continue till the song ends so if you pick a long and beaty song at hard or above, prepare for a beating.
4:Beat Hazard Ultra DLC
Currently there are 2 version on sale on steam, the normal edition and the one bundled with the DLC Beat Hazard Ultra. Genrally speaking, get the bundle. it includes even more bosses, more enemy types, more perk and generally more of everything that the classic beat hazard doesnt have! Also the effects are shinier in the DLC so yeah, poor retina.
Conclusion.
Great game with friends or by yourself. hopefully drunken friends that way you can play those super weird music as you blast spaceship in tune to the beat. Definitely a thumbs up.
[TIPS]
Cant find a hard enough music? Insane too easy? Go use white noises as the music. Dont say i didnt warn you.

As turn based strategy games go, XCOM is a fun one. Aliens have invaded, and it is up to your secret military organisation to kick them off this rock. And you do that with a combination of clever tactics, superior firepower, autopsy reports, and interrogations.
As you capture and torture more alien visitors, and as you study more of their tech, you can seriously upgrade Earth's defenses. For example, at the start of the invasion, you have fighter jets, with basic missiles. Later on, your pilots are flying the Firestorm, highly advanced fighter ship which is more or less alien in origin, and can be equipped with such awesome firepower as the plasma cannon, or the fusion lance.
Your weapons and armour similarly are upgraded as you progress through the research tree, starting with basic weapons as you might find these days, upgrading to lasers, and then plasma weapons.
So, what are you waiting for? Go kick some alien butt.

Looking for a new way to spice up your music listening sessions? If you answered yes, then this is the game for you! Because 'Beat Hazard' is basically just a music visualizer with lives. And if you don't have enough lives to make it through the song, well, then you don't hear the end of that song; it's as simple as that. Finally something that makes listening to music more challenging! Ugh, we've seen this game a thousand times before, literally, there are a thousand other versions of this game out there already. Like 'Asteroids, Geometry Wars, Darius Twin, Giga Wing, 1943, LifeForce, Gradius, Raiden, Super Stardust, etc. You get the point, there are a lot of spaceship shooty games on the market.
Sad to say however, 'Beat Hazard' adds nothing new to this already saturated genre other than allowing us to play along to our favorite songs. But we could already do that by listening to our favorite songs while playing better versions of this game with the sound off. It was a nice attempt but 'Beat Hazard' falls really flat, no pun intended. There is just too much going on visually, even when turning the effects down half-way, and sometimes it's much too difficult to distinguish from what will and will not hurt you as debris flies all about. Not to mention the graphics look very cheap, especially the spaceship, and with a game with so many visual effects, it seriously hinders the experience, at least for me.
Overall there is still some fun to be had here, but pick 'Beat Hazard' up on sale, because ten bucks is just too much to pay for this generic pile of visual poppycock. The 'Survival Mode' is the one aspect that may keep you coming back, but other than that, avoid this game for something better like one of the titles mentioned above, because honestly, the one thing this game promises to do; power itself with your music, it doesn't even do very well.

The Legend of Eisenwald is one of my favorite games. This game however, does a disservice to the spirit of Eisenwald. This stand alone DLC is just a single map scenario, where the devs use the toolset to crack a political joke about the 2016 election. FTL is rad rouge-like-like which presents you with battle and narrative scenarios which one might liken to Star Trek. A Rebellion armada is conquering the galaxy and only the sensitive inforamtion you carry aboard your ship can turn the tide of battle in favor of The Federation. FTL is broken up into a couple of different systems that provide hours of fun and experimentation. Upgrade your ship by collecting scrap from battle or from different types of encounters. Then spend that scrap on your ship systems like shields, weapons, life support, or even better doors. The combat system fits incredibly well with the theme and makes a vairety of strategies vialble for success. For example, you can use missle type weapons that by pass shileds, laser weapons that have infinte ammunition, ion cannons that disrupt systems without doing damage, automated bots that chip at enemey shileds, teleporters for boarding ships, or any combination of the previoulsy mentioned.
On top of the great mechanics, FTL provides narrative choices that are so much more than basic black and white morality calls. Do you want your crew to investigate a mysterious derlict ship or should they blow it up and collect the valuable leftover scrap? Slavers with supeiror fire power have cornered you and are demanding you turn over one of your crew members in order for you to continue unharmed. It's up to you wether or not you send that crew member to his fate or stand up to the pirates, all while the balance of the galaxy rests on your shoulders.
Customize and command your ship throughout the cosmos, meet all sorts of new alien races, and experience all the cool nuances of this awesome world created by Subset Games - you won't regret it! Play FTL: Faster Than Light!

Pro's
Even though it's a really solid RPG, like 8/10, the real pull of this game is it's exceptional art style and good characters and story. The combat uses a really fun system, where by hitting an enemy with a skill or attack while there casting you can bump them back on the timeline, effectivey making them miss a turn, but beware, they can also do this to you which adds layers of depth to the game. The game uses the same engin as Rayman Legends, making the game breathtakingly beautiful. The orchestral soundtrack is also briliant, sounding wonderfully melancholy.
Cons

On top of that the skill tree system, while I like the customization for every character it gives you, is rather cluttered, making it hard to have each character be exactly what you want them to be.

Just from 1 hour of gameplay, I can honestly say that buying this game was a terriffic choice! The game is exactly as advertised, a JRPG that takes various tropes and punches them in the face! The story is fairly good too. Otakus would probably understand what I mean when I say the game is like Hetalia but for the Video Game industry. The game's four main characters are all based on the 4 major gaming console manufacturers: Sega (Sega Neptune), Sony (Playstation), Nintendo (Wii), and Microsoft (XBox), and are in the midst of waging a war literally called "The Console War" in the world of "Gameindustri." Yeah, that's how this game rolls and thats just the beginning.
This being a JRPG, the game has an opening like a traditonal anime and the opening is very good too. Be warned, the majority if not the entirety of the main cast are female and most appear to be the typical teenaged anime characters and there is some noticable "jiggle physics" on some of the characters. Just a fair heads up.
Gameplay wise, keyboard controls are a bit dodgy. The game is meant to be played with a controller (which actually makes more sense considering the premice of the game itself) but has rebindable keys for keyboard. I recommend using an XBox 360 Controller (wired) as a fast alternative workaround.
In terms of combat, the game is turn based but with an interesting twist. You can move the characters around within a certain radius, putting their target into a blue targeting box in front of them. You can target multiple enemies this way especially if they're clustered together. The enemy won't move until it's their turn too. One thing mouse and keyboard has an advantage over controler is that you can more carefully turn your characters so you can line up accurate attacks.

I found this to be a solid and charming RPG.  Dont let the ubisoft brand fool you.  I played for a bit over 18 hrs and enjoyed this game quite a bit.
The gameplay is, if anything, a bit too easy in the same way that Kingdom Hearts is.  If you are modestly competent almost every fight wont be challenging even at the harder difficulty setting, but it's still enjoyable to play.  Combat is similar to an ATB system with actions being queued up on a time bar before being performed.  Some actions can be interrupted, others affect a characters turn in some way, allowing for some finesse and control on the part of the player.  This comes along with an ATB-independent heal the player can perform with his mouse cursor that uses its own slowly recharging resource, and for some reason I found the balance between the two fairly enjoyable and engaging.  In the more tense fights, healing characters at the right moments was crucial along with timing when you would be able to heal again after expending all of your resource was fairly important.  Characters are diverse and can fit varied roles in combat, enough that I didnt feel like I should stick to just a few that I might like.  Outside of combat puzzles are fairly easy and nothing too complex or ingenious comes up, and there is some light exploration and backtracking for rewards you can do as well.  Exploration does kind of fall flat a little because they give you complete exploration powers very shortly into the game, but its also not a metroidvania title so calling it a 'missed opportunity' or like doesn't quite fit.  Jamming RPG, light crafting mechanics, skill trees, exploration, etc all into a game is a lot and eventually you'd end up with feature bloat.
The story has a kind of light fairytail whimsy to it, in the way that some aspects are obscured or ambiguous or mean to be accepted prima facie.  It works out for the most part, and the way they presented the world and characters was satisfying.  and had some nice twists too. Some people dont like the rhyming dialogue, but I did.  I liked most all of the characters too, even a few I expected not to on first glance like Rubella.  I think if anything one of the problems they had was the sin of taking away a character from the player whom one might have expended permanent stat upgrade consumables on, and also in introducing one character too late and letting a few others kind of flounder a bit.  Still, the ones that did get time in the story were nice.
I'd highly recommend it, it's not a top 5 title but it definitely went into my favorites.

One of the best games of the past 10 years.
Lets start with the story. Aliens invade...and they arn't here to hand out cupcakes. It is your job to stop the aliens.
How do you stop them?  You are in charge of an organization called XCOM which is funded by 16 countries.  They have all put their faith in your skilled stratigic mind to find a way to combat a threat that is completly unknown. As Commander of XCOM you will have full freedom to recruit soldiers from the worlds best to fight and most likly die for the future of humanity.
Your soldiers will be important for actually neutralizing the threat on the ground via a turn based combat system with the varied and deadly enemies that will be thrown at you. Once the aliens attempt an abduction or land a UFO in a country you will be able to dispatch a squad of up to 6 soliders to handle the situation.  You move your soldiers around a square grid system in various envirnments.  Make sure you keep them in cover if enemies are visible or they will be gunned down quite quickly. Yoy have 4 different classes of soldiers to handle the threat. An Assualt class which is useful for flanking enemies because it can move 2 times in a turn and still attack( flanking shots have a decetn chance to critical hit which can kill most early to mid game enemies).  Heavy class carries a LMG and rocket launcher which can be used to deal heavy damage from mid range. Support classes lack the firepower of the others but can thorw down a smoke screen  and take advantage of med kits to keep your squad in the fight longer.  Snipers are self explanitory and inflict damage from a distance, and while they start out weak a fully ranked up sniper can wreck havoc.  As Soldiers complete mission and gain experience they rank up allowing you to select from various new abilites at each rank to somewhat tailer that soldier how you want. However your troops can easily be killed which creates an interesting dynamic where you want to get experience for them so they can be your A-team, but the ever present spectre of permadeath creates a constant tension in combat.  This is one place where the game shines but also one of its greatest weaknesses since you can get by a mission with one or two of your best troops getting killed, but you should just save-scum and reload if it seems hopeless, at least on your first couple of playthroughs of the game.  The main reason is that rookie soldiers are almost completely useless in a serious fight after a certain point in the game when the aliens start deploying there best units.  You can get around this by investing in robotic units you will unlock at a ceratin point.
When your soldiers are victorious in the field you are rewarding with alien corpses which your science team at base can use to learn more about the enemy, alien materials and weapon pieces that allow your engineering to upgrade the equipment and weapons you soldiers can bring to bear.  You also will have to build new buidlings to your headquartes which you will need for the upgrades and research I mentioned as well as expanding your satalite coverage, which you should prioritze since it will get you a lot more money since running a global defense organization is not cheap. You also will manage a fleet of intercepters to shoot down enemy UFOs( They will also need upgrades to remain effective since the flying saucers will soon become less frequent and they enemy will deploy heavier ships).  In my opinion the interceptor gameplay could have been a bit deeper like the tactical missions, but it at the very least doesnt get it the way.  From your base you will recieve requests for help from countries, but you won't be able to respond to all of them, and the countries you didn't help will have an increase in their panic rating. If the panic rating gets too high they will leave the XCOM project, taking their funding with them. Lose 8 countries and it is game over. This does the job of creating tension and a constant sense of dread.
Overall this is a great game and makes it feel like your are really in charge of saving the world. The interplay between the tactical level on the missions and the stratigic level on the base managment is most likly why this game turned out so great.  My last bit of critisism is the difficulty curve, in that it starts easy, gets very difficult in the middle, and becomes insanely easy by the end.  This is because once your soldiers have the best armor, weapons and abilites they can make mince meat of anything the enemy can throw at you for the most part.  At this point you will likly have access to the final level which is the only thing left to do at that point. But even if the end of the journy is a bit lackluster( nowhere near as bad as Far Cry 3) the overall journey is excellent due to randomized levels and enemy placement will be unique for each playtrhough.

Banner Saga is a turn-based strategy RPG, and the first in a trilogy of games. A good way to think of it is a mix between Oregon Trail and a Norse High-Fantasy version of XCOM.
This game is just a joy to experience, with its beautiful artwork and score and excellent worldbuilding. Characterization is great and the story unfolds at a reasonable pace for getting immersed into journey. There's quite a bit of backstory and a LOT of reading, but diving into everything with no idea what to expect turned out to be a truly rewarding experience. There's so much depth here, and it's a blast to watch everything unfold.
It's just a great game - challenging enough to make you care, relentless enough to make you try, but not so brutal as to be overly unfair or difficult. I can't recommend it highly enough.
